newsitem.title: USA: L.A. balcony-sex death-plunge ruled a homicide.
newsitem.headline: L.A. balcony-sex death-plunge ruled a homicide.

text.p: The death of a woman who plunged from a hotel balcony while apparently engaging in sex has been ruled a homicide, and detectives have reopened a murder investigation, officials said on Thursday.
A spokesman for the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department said it was in contact with investigators in Houston, Texas, where the victim, Sandra Orellana, had lived.

She fell to her death last Nov. 13 from the balcony of a hotel in a Los Angeles suburb. Her boss, Robert Salazar, whom she was accompanying on a business trip, told police at the time that she fell accidentally while the couple made love on the balcony of her room.

Salazar, 33, who went back to his room and slept without reporting the fall, was taken into custody at the time. He was later released and returned home to Texas. Local news reports have said he had left his underwear in Orellana's room.
On Thursday, the Los Angeles County Coroner's office said it had determined the 27-year-old Orellana's injuries were consistent with being pushed rather than falling.
A week after the death, police dropped a mannequin from the same balcony in an effort to duplicate the fall. They determined the spot where she landed was not consistent with an accidental fall.
Coroner's spokesman Scott Carrier said on Thursday, "She had a lot of abrasions and lacerations that were consistent with a drop as opposed to a jumping situation."
"It would have required assistance (to get over the railing) because of her stature," Carrier said. It was therefore determined to be "an assisted drop," hence the homicide classification, he said.
A spokeswoman for the district attorney's office said no case against Salazar had been presented by detectives. The sheriff's spokesman said detectives were still investigating.
